30-5-2002.--The following Ordinance made by the Governor of Sindh is hereby
published for general information: --
3. Incorporation.---There
shall be established at Karachi an Institute to be called the Newports
Institute of Communications and Economics consisting of-
(i)
the members of such councils, committees and other bodies as the Board may establish;
(ii)
the teachers and students of the Institute and its constituent units;
(iii)
the Chairman, the Vice-Chairman, the Deans and other members of the Board; and
(iv)
such other officers and members of the staff as may from time to time be specified by the Board.
(b) The Institute shall be a body

name sue and be sued.

sections.shortTitle: Newport Institute of Communication and Economics Ordinance 2002
sections.description:
Powers and Functions of the Newports Institute

NEWPORT INSTITUTE OF COMMUNICATION AND ECONOMICS ORDINANCE, 2002
NEWPORT INSTITUTE
OF COMMUNICATION AND ECONOMICS ORDINANCE, 2002
ORDINANCE XVI OF 2002
An Ordinance to
provide for the establishment of an Institute at Karachi known as the Newports
of institute of Communications and Economics
[Gazette of Sindh,
Extraordinary, Part I, 30th May, 2002]
No. S. Legis.I(16)/2002, dated
30-5-2002.--The following Ordinance made by the Governor of Sindh is hereby
published for general information: --
4. Powers and Functions of the
Newports Institute. ---(1) The Institute shall have the powers
(a) to provide for instructions
and training in such branches of learning
as it may deem fit, and to make provision for research demonstration and other
services, and for the advancement and dissemination of knowledge;
(b) to admit and examine
students;
(c) to hold examinations and
confer or award degrees, diploma, certificates and other academic distinctions
on and to persons who have passed its examination under the prescribed
conditions;
(d) to select and promote
faculties;
(e) to confer, honorary degrees;
(f) to prescribe courses of
studies in such branches of learning as the Institute may determine;
(g) to pursue research;
(h) to establish and support
other facilities for education, training research;
(i) to enter into agreements,
contacts and arrangements with universities, organizations, institutions,
bodies and individuals for the purpose of carrying out its functions and
activities;
(j) to decide teaching methods
and strategies in order to ensure the most effective educational and training
programmes;
(k) to demand and receive such
fees and other charges as it may determine, provided that ten percent. of the
students will be granted free-ship or financial support on the basis of need
cum merit.
(2) The powers and functions
under subsection (1) shall be exercised and performed subject to general
control and directions of the Government.

in the Institute. ---(a) The academic programmers of the Institute

(b) The Institute shall associate

(c) No degree shall be granted
unless a student has passed an examination in Islamic Studies and Pakistan

Visitation

NEWPORT INSTITUTE OF COMMUNICATION AND ECONOMICS ORDINANCE, 2002
NEWPORT INSTITUTE
OF COMMUNICATION AND ECONOMICS ORDINANCE, 2002
ORDINANCE XVI OF 2002
An Ordinance to
provide for the establishment of an Institute at Karachi known as the Newports

[Gazette of Sindh,
Extraordinary, Part I, 30th May, 2002]
No. S. Legis.I(16)/2002, dated
30-5-2002.--The following Ordinance made by the Governor of Sindh is hereby
published for general information: --
10. Visitation. ---(a)
The Patron may cause an inspection or inquiry to be made on his own motion in respect of any matter connected with the
affairs of the Institute and shall, from time to time, direct any person or
persons to inquire or carry out inspection of-
(i) the Institute, its buildings, Laboratories, libraries and other
facilities;
(ii) any institution, department or hostel maintained by the Institute;
(iii) the adequacy of financial and human resources of the institute;
(iv) the teaching, research, curriculum, examination and other matters
of the Institute; and
(v) such other matters as may specified by him.
(b) The Patron shall communicate to the Board his views with regard to
the results of the visitation and shall, after ascertaining the views of the
Board, advise the Board on the action to be taken by it.
(c) The Board shall, within such time as may be specified by the
Patron, communicate to him such action, if any, as has been taken or may 1w
proposed to be taken upon the results of visitation.
(d) Where the Board does not
within the time specified, take action to the satisfaction of the Patron, the
Patron may issue such directions as he deems fit and the Board shall comply
with all directions.
(e) The Patron shall have full
powers to take any action, as he may deem fit against the Institute, including
withdrawal of charter and its closure.

Chairman

NEWPORT INSTITUTE OF COMMUNICATION AND ECONOMICS ORDINANCE, 2002
NEWPORT INSTITUTE
OF COMMUNICATION AND ECONOMICS ORDINANCE, 2002
ORDINANCE XVI OF 2002
An Ordinance to

No. S. Legis.I(16)/2002, dated
30-5-2002.--The following Ordinance made by the Governor of Sindh is hereby
published for general information: --
11. Chairman.---(a) The
Chairman shall be appointed by the Patron from a panel recommended by the
Society for a period of four years.
(b) The Vice-Chairman shall be
appointed by the Chairman on the recommendations of the Board on such, terms
and conditions as may be prescribed.
(c) The Chairman shall in the
absence of the Patron preside at the convocation.
(d) If the Chairman is satisfied
that the proceedings of any Authority or orders of any officer are not in
accordance with the provisions of this Ordinance, the statutes, the regulations
or the rules, he may, after calling upon such Authority or officer to show
cause why such proceedings should clot be annulled, by order in writing, annual
such proceedings or orders.
(e) The Chairman may remove any
person from the membership of any Authority if such person-
(i)
has become of unsound mind; or
(ii)
has been incapacitated to function as member of such Authority; or
(iii)
has been convicted by Court of law for an offence involving moral turpitude or has been found indulging in any
activity against the interest of the Institute;
(iv)
Should the Chairman be incapacitated from acting as such due to absence or any other cause, the Vice-Chairman or
nominee of the Chairman shall act for him.

sections.shortTitle: Newport Institute of Communication and Economics Ordinance 2002
sections.description:
Terms and Conditions of Appointment of Rector

NEWPORT INSTITUTE OF COMMUNICATION AND ECONOMICS ORDINANCE, 2002
NEWPORT INSTITUTE
OF COMMUNICATION AND ECONOMICS ORDINANCE, 2002
ORDINANCE XVI OF 2002
An Ordinance to
provide for the establishment of an Institute at Karachi known as the Newports
of institute of Communications and Economics
[Gazette of Sindh,
Extraordinary, Part I, 30th May, 2002]
No. S. Legis.I(16)/2002, dated
30-5-2002.--The following Ordinance made by the Governor of Sindh is hereby
published for general information: --
12. Terms and Conditions of
Appointment of Rector.---(a) The Rector shall be an eminent scholar of
national or international repute and an educationist of distinction and shall
be appointed by the Chairman on the recommendation of the Board for a period of
four years on such terms and conditions as the Board may determine.
(b) The Rector shall be the Chief
Academic and administrative ;officer of the Institute and shall be responsible
for the implementation of the decision of the Board and for the execution of
the programme of the institute in accordance with the guidelines and policies
formulated by the Board.
(c) The Rector shall also have
powers-
(i)
to submit plans of work and budget estimates of the Institute to the Board for considerations and approval;
(ii)
to direct the activities connected with the execution of programmes for instructions, training, research,
service to the community;
(iii)
to authorize expenditure provided for in the approved budget and to re-appropriate funds within the same
major head of expenditure and report it to the
Board in the next meeting;
(iv)
to sanction and re-appropriate an amount not exceeding one lac rupees for an unforeseen item not provided for in the
budget and report it to the Board in the next
meeting;
(v)
to appoint, with the approval of the Board, teachers, officers and members of the staff of the Institute and such
other persons as may be necessary in accordance with policies and procedures approved by the Board so as to ensure
the highest intellectual and moral
qualities in the persons appointed;
(vi)
to submit to the Board, in accordance with the rules of procedure, reports on the activities of the Institute and
the execution of the plans of work;
(vii)
to create temporary posts for a period not exceeding six months; and
(viii)
to undertake any work assigned by the Board;

13. Board.---(a) The Board
shall consist of the following-
(i)
the Chairman;
(ii)
a Judge of the High Court of Sindh nominated by the Chief Justice;
(iii)
Chairman of the Commission or his nominee;
(iv)
Secretary Education or his nominee not below the rank of an Additional Secretary;
(v)

(c) No act or proceedings of the
Board shall be invalid by reasons only of the existence of a vacancy in, or any

sections.shortTitle: Newport Institute of Communication and Economics Ordinance 2002
sections.description:
Powers and Functions of the Board

NEWPORT INSTITUTE OF COMMUNICATION AND ECONOMICS ORDINANCE, 2002
NEWPORT INSTITUTE
OF COMMUNICATION AND ECONOMICS ORDINANCE, 2002
ORDINANCE XVI OF 2002
An Ordinance to
provide for the establishment of an Institute at Karachi known as the Newports
of institute of Communications and Economics
[Gazette of Sindh,
Extraordinary, Part I, 30th May, 2002]
No. S. Legis.I(16)/2002, dated
30-5-2002.--The following Ordinance made by the Governor of Sindh is hereby
published for general information: --
14. Powers and Functions of
the Board.---The Board shall exercise the power and perform the functions
as follows:--
(i)
to hold, control and administer the property, funds and resources of the Institute and raise funds for the
purpose of the Institute upon such security as may be required under regulations;
(ii)
undertake responsibility for the financial viability of the Institute including
responsibility for ensuring
effectiveness of its operations their continuity and preservation of the autonomy of the Institute;
(iii)
to consider and pass the resolution of the annual report, plan work statement of accounts and the annual budget estimates;
(iv) to formulate or
approve the principles, policies and plans governing the activities and operations of the
Institute so as to facilitate research teaching and other academic work;
(v)
to make statutes and approve rules and regulations;
(vi)
to have prepared and revised from time to time rules and regulation for the efficient and effective operation of the
Institute;
(vii)
to create a component of the Institute such as faculties, departments and institutes under its jurisdiction and to
constitute such standing committees, councils
and other administrative or academic advisory bodies as it deems necessary, and review their work;
(viii)
to approve plans of work and annual budget of the Institute;
(ix)
to call for and consider reports relating to the activities of the Institute
and the execution of the plans of work and to direct the Rector to furnish
information relating to any matter
specified by the Board;
(x) to create such
academic or administrative posts as it may deem necessary and to approve appointment to such posts;
(xi) to constitute
committees or sub-committees as it may deem necessary;
(xii)
to take all such initiative as it may consider necessary for the efficient and effective management and functioning of the
Institute;
(xiii)
to appoint teachers and other employees on the recommendations of the Selection Board, and
(xiv)
to delegate its powers to any authority or officer including the Rector or a Committee.

published for general information: --
15. Meeting of the Board.---(a)
The Board shall meet at least twice a year on the dates to be fixed by the
Vice-Chairman, with approval of Chairman, provided that a special meeting may
be called at any time by the Chairman or on the request by not less than five
members of the Board to consider any matter of urgent nature.
(b) In the case of a special
meeting not less than ten clear days notice shall be given to the members of
the Board, and the agenda of the meeting shall be restricted to the matter for
which the special meeting is called.
(c) The quorum for a meeting of
the board shall be one-half of its members fraction being counted as one.
(d) The decisions of the Board
shall be expressed in terms of the views of the majority and voting of the members present and if the members
are equally divided, the Chairman shall have the power to exercise a casting
vote.

NEWPORT INSTITUTE OF COMMUNICATION AND ECONOMICS ORDINANCE, 2002

OF COMMUNICATION AND ECONOMICS ORDINANCE, 2002
ORDINANCE XVI OF 2002
An Ordinance to

No. S. Legis.I(16)/2002, dated

published for general information: --
17. Institute Fund, Audit and
Accounts.---(a) The Institute shall have a Fund to which shall be credited
income from fees, donations, trusts, bequests, endowments, grants, contribution
and any other source.
(b) No contributions, donation or
grant, which may directly or indirectly involve any immediate or subsequent
financial liability of the institute or which may involve an activity not
included in its programmes for the time being shall be accepted without the
prior approval of the Board.
(c) The accounts of the Institute
shall be maintained in such form .end in such manner as be prescribed by rules.
(d) The accounts of the Institute
shall be audited each year within four months of the closing of the financial
year by a Chartered Accountant appointed by the Board.
(e) The accounts, together with
the report of the auditor thereon, shall be submitted to the Board for
approval.
(f) The auditor's report shall
certify that the auditor has complied with the standards of audit and
certification laid down by the Institute of Chartered Accountant of Pakistan.

18. The Academic Council.---(a)
The Academic Council shall consist of--
(i)
the Rector who shall be the Chairman;
(ii)
all the Deans;
(iii)
all the Heads of the Teaching Departments;
(iv)
all Professors and Associate Professor of `the Institute;
(v)
a nominee of the Education Secretary not below the rank of Deputy Secretary, the Regional Director of the Education
(Colleges) and the Director of Technical Education
concerned;
(vi)
two Assistant Professors and two Lecturers to be nominated by the Board;
(vii)
three persons eminent in the arts, the sciences and the professionals, one from each category to be nominated by the
Board;
(viii)
Adviser, (Academics), of the Commission, or his nominee; and
(ix)
the Registrar, who shall act as its Secretary.
(b) Members appointed by
nomination shall hold office for a period of three years.
(c) The quorum for a meeting of
the Academic Council shall be one third of the total number of members; a
fraction being counted as one.

sections.shortTitle: Newport Institute of Communication and Economics Ordinance 2002
sections.description:
Powers and Duties of the Academic Council

NEWPORT INSTITUTE OF COMMUNICATION AND ECONOMICS ORDINANCE, 2002
NEWPORT INSTITUTE
OF COMMUNICATION AND ECONOMICS ORDINANCE, 2002
ORDINANCE XVI OF 2002
An Ordinance to
provide for the establishment of an Institute at Karachi known as the Newports
of institute of Communications and Economics
[Gazette of Sindh,
Extraordinary, Part I, 30th May, 2002]
No. S. Legis.I(16)/2002, dated
30-5-2002.--The following Ordinance made by the Governor of Sindh is hereby
published for general information: --
19. Powers and Duties of the
Academic Council.---(a) The Academic Council shall be the academic body of
the Institute and shall subject to the provisions of the Ordinance and the
statutes, have the powers to lay down proper standards of instructions,
research, publication, examinations and to regulate and promote the academic
life of the Institute.
(b) Without prejudice to the
generally of the foregoing powers and subject to the provisions of this
Ordinance and the statutes, the Academic Council shall have the powers--
(i)
to advise the Board on academic matters;
(ii)
to regulate the conduct of-teaching, research, publication and examination;
(iii)
to regulate the admission of students to the courses of studies and examinations in the Institute,
(iv)
to regulate the conduct and discipline of the students of the Institute;
(v)
to propose to the Board schemes for the constitution and organisation of the Faculties and Teaching Department;
(vi)
to consider and formulate proposals of teaching and research in the Institute for the planning and development;
(vii)
to prescribe the course of studies, the syllabi and the outlines of tests for
all examinations subject to
the approval of the Board;
(viii)
to regulate the award of studentships, scholarships, exhibitions, medals and prizes;

An Ordinance to

[Gazette of Sindh,

No. S. Legis.I(16)/2002, dated
30-5-2002.--The following Ordinance made by the Governor of Sindh is hereby
published for general information: --
24. First Statutes. ---Notwithstanding
anything to the contrary contained in this Ordinance, the First Statutes shall
be deemed to be the statutes framed under this Ordinance and shall continue to
remain in force until amended or repealed or till such time as new statutes are
framed in accordance with the provisions of this Ordinance.
FIRST STATUTES
(See section 24)
1. The Institute shall, include
the following faculties and such other faculties as may be prescribed:--
(a)
Faculty of Computer Science.
(b)
Faculty of Business Administration.
(c)
Faculty of Law.
(d)
Faculty of Social Sciences.
(e)
Faculty of Regional area Studies and Foreign Languages.
2. Board of Faculty.---(a) There shall be a Board of each Faculty,
,.v hich shall consist of--
(i)
the Dean of the Faculty;
(ii)
the Professors and the Heads of the Teaching Department in the faculty;
(iii)
one member other than Professors and Head of each Teaching Department to be nominated by the head;
(iv)
two teachers to be nominated by the Academic Council by reason of their specialized knowledge of the subjects which,
though not assigned to the faculty, but
has in the opinion of the Academic Council important bearing on the subject assigned to the faculty;
(v)
two experts in the relevant field from outside the Institute to be appointed by
the Board; and
(vi)
one member to be nominated by the Rector.
(b) The member other than
ex-officio members shall hold office for a period of three years;
(c) The quorum for a meeting of
the Board of a Faculty shall be one-half of the total number of members, a
fraction being counted as one.
3. Functions of the Board of
Faculty.---The Board of Faculty shall, subject to the general control of
the Academic Council and the Board have the powers to-
(a) co-ordinate the teaching and
research work in the subject assigned to the Faculty;
(b) scrutinize the
recommendations of the Board of Studies comprising the Faculty with regard to
the appointment of paper-setters and examiners, for graduate and post-graduate
examinations and to forward the panels of suitable paper-setter and examiners
for each examination to the Rector.
(c) consider any other academic
matter relating to the Faculty and report thereon to the Academic Council;
(d) prepare a comprehensive
annual report regarding the performance of each department, comprising the
Faculty for presentation to the Academic Council; and
(e) perform such other functions
as may be prescribed by statutes.
4. Dean.---(a) There shall
be Dean of each Faculty who shall be the Chairman and Convenor of the Board of
Faculty.
(b) The Dean shall be appointed
by the Board from amongst the three most senior Professors of the Faculty on
the recommendation of the Rector and shall hold office for a period of three
years and shall be eligible for re-appointment.
(c) The Dean shall have such powers
and duties as may be prescribed by the Board on the recommendations of the
Rector.
5. Teaching Departments and
Heads of the Departments. ---(a) There shall be a Teaching Department for
each subject or a group of subject, as may be prescribed by regulations and
each Teaching Department shall be headed by the Head of Department.
(b) The Head of a Teaching
Department, shall be appointed by the Board on the recommendations of the
Rector from amongst three senior most Professors or Associate Professors other
than Professors already working as Dean for a period of three years and shall
be eligible for re-appointment:
